assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1995 Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with laser-cooled trapped ions turned quantum computation from an abstract idea into a concrete physical architecture, and their later cold-atom and Rydberg-based proposals defined analogue and digital quantum simulation. The ideas are original, clear and have shaped experiments in several platforms, including ones close to my own field of circuit and waveguide QED.
assessment.attribution: The credited pair is natural and compact: they are the decisive theorists for the ion-gate proposal and for the optical-lattice Hubbard-model proposal. Experimental credit (Wineland-Monroe-Blatt-Wunderlich-style ion gates) is partly covered by the earlier 2012 prize, which makes a theory-only prize coherent.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of experimental confirmation with ions, atoms and other platforms, and a stable interpretation. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to couple them with experimental quantum-simulation leaders (the Bloch-Greiner line, entry B015) rather than recognise them alone.
I rely on my own recollection of the 1995 and 1998 proposals and have not verified details of priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error-correcting codes, fault-tolerance thresholds and topological codes are the conceptual basis for any scalable quantum computer; as director of a quantum-technology programme I regard full-scale error correction as the central technical requirement. Shor's 1995 code and Kitaev's toric/surface-code ideas are original and have had lasting influence on experiments, including recent below-threshold demonstrations.
assessment.attribution: Credit is distributed: Shor, Steane, Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme, Preskill, Aharonov and Ben-Or and others all made decisive contributions. Among the supplied names, Shor (first code, factoring-linked fault tolerance) and Kitaev (topological fault tolerance, surface-code lineage) are the most defensible pair; Steane's independent code is important but a prize would have to be limited to three.
assessment.maturity: Theory is mature, and experimental demonstrations are now arriving but are still early for logical-qubit performance at scale. Timing is acceptable but the experimental payoff is not yet complete.
uncertainties: The factoring algorithm is separate from error correction and may be viewed as a distinct discovery that complicates the framing.
Real-world impact on useful computation is still unproven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong, controllable coupling between a superconducting qubit and a microwave resonator routine, providing dispersive readout, two-qubit coupling and the architecture used by most superconducting processors. The idea is original and its impact is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 theory proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the first experiment (Wallraff et al., 2004) split credit among four credited names; Schoelkopf and Wallraff are decisive experimentally, Blais and Girvin theoretically. I have a close professional interest in this area and would flag that, and the choice of three among four is unresolved. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling was adjacent but not identical.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and independently confirmed in many laboratories. Timing is reasonable, though a second superconducting-circuit prize so soon after 2025 may be seen as premature by some members.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize may weigh against it in the same field.
Who is left out among Girvin, Blais, Schoelkopf and Wallraff is a genuine allocation problem.
My professional proximity to this field could bias my view.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and the ensuing quantum key distribution, together with the framing of quantum information protocols, opened a field with real applications and deep foundational links. The originality and long-term influence are clear, and Ekert's entanglement-based protocol is also significant.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the originators of BB84 and of quantum teleportation (with others); Ekert's 1991 protocol is independent and conceptually distinct. A three-person prize is possible, but I propose the pair as the cleanest attribution.
assessment.maturity: Experiments and commercial systems exist, and the physics is stable. The discovery is old enough that recognition is timely if not overdue.
uncertainties: Part of the impact is information-theoretic and may be judged as outside physics proper.
Teleportation credit (Bennett, Brassard and co-authors) might need separate treatment.
Practical security of implementations is not the same as the underlying theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Loss-DiVincenzo proposal for spin qubits in quantum dots and its experimental realisation with high-fidelity single- and two-qubit gates in silicon form a coherent theory-to-experiment story for a scalable solid-state qubit platform. Significance is high and the semiconductor route is a credible alternative to superconducting circuits.
assessment.attribution: Loss and DiVincenzo for the 1998 proposal and Vandersypen for leading experimental demonstrations is a plausible configuration, though Kouwenhoven, Petta, Yacoby, Marcus, Morello, Dzurak and others contributed essential experiments.
assessment.maturity: Experimental progress is strong, but scaled-up processors are not yet demonstrated, so impact is still developing.
uncertainties: Experimental credit is spread over many groups and the three chosen may be contested.
Long-term competitiveness against other qubit modalities is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire materials as a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics, with very large follow-on activity.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key theoretical prediction in 2011; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental discoveries. This triple matches the decisive contributions, with Cao and others as junior authors not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups in a short time, but microscopic understanding of the superconductivity and correlated states remains incomplete.
uncertainties: Interpretation of the superconducting mechanism is unsettled.
Possible desire to wait for lasting technological or conceptual consequence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, based on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's implementation at extreme precision, have reached uncertainties near 10^-18 and enable tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. The importance and the measurement clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice in 2001-2003, and Ye's group made the leading accuracy demonstrations, giving a clear and fair two-person configuration. Ye's overlap with other candidates is a minor consideration.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently reproduced; the SI second redefinition is still pending but the scientific case is well established.
uncertainties: Hall and Hansch were recognised in 2005 for frequency combs, which some may regard as overlap.
Whether a redefinition of the second will change the weighting is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by its observation in HgTe quantum wells, established a new class of materials with topologically protected edge states and broad influence in condensed matter and quantum technology thinking.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the 2005 prediction, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposed HgTe, and Molenkamp's group observed it in 2007; Hasan's 3D work is also credited in this entry. The three chosen cover the earliest decisive theory and experiment, but Zhang is not available among the names (deceased) and allocation is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, reproduced widely, and mainstream in textbooks. Recognition is timely or somewhat overdue, but sharing with the separate 3D topological-insulator line is unresolved.
uncertainties: Splitting between 2D and 3D topological insulators and with the BHZ proposal is unresolved.
Allocation among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp and Hasan is disputed.
